correctness.rationale: An insertion-vector history is uniquely the pair of retained source positions among four; this yields the exact six-embedding count formula. For distinct centers, a four-letter output with >=2 symbols not in their common center alphabet cannot embed both, so each intersection equals a constant plus (q-s) times the one-outsider constant. Complete canonical 13-pattern enumeration yields exact coefficients, with the 8q-5 maximum strictly above all other patterns for all admissible q>=2. A standalone stdlib checker reconstructs the finite sums, tests the symbolic reduction, and exhaustively checks all unordered pairs for q=2..6. The channel threshold equals one plus the largest multiset intersection. Assumptions and quantifiers are explicitly fixed; finite tests are not used as the all-q proof.

value.rationale: The exact length-two/two-insertion case is the first simultaneous step beyond the regimes length one or insertion count one solved in the directly motivating literature, a naturally selected boundary rather than an arbitrary parameter slice. The theorem determines the operational worst-case channel count for every alphabet, not just an individual example, and classifies all worst-case center pairs. The symbolic outside-letter reduction exposes a stable affine dependence on q and a one-unit gap to the next closest pattern, making the result structurally informative for multiset synchronization reconstruction.
